correctness.rationale: The connected Laplacians are positive definite on the orthogonal complement of the constants, and the trace of their inverses has positive second variation in every nonzero symmetric direction. Simple edges make the weight-to-Laplacian map injective; disconnection gives an infinite limit, and uniform scaling uses the full budget. Thus the global minimizer exists, is unique and must be invariant under rotations, including at the two endpoints. An independent endpoint evaluation is as follows. For the unit n-cycle let mu_k be its nonzero eigenvalues, S=sum(1/mu_k)=(n^2-1)/12, and J(d)=sum((2-2cos(2pi kd/n))/mu_k^2). Parallel-path resistance d(n-d)/n and its Fourier form give J(d+1)-2J(d)+J(d-1)=2S-d(n-d). With zero boundary values at d=0,n, this gives J(d)=d(n-d)[d(n-d)+2]/12. Thus leaving the first-only endpoint is unfavorable exactly at t>=J(2)/S=4(n-2)/(n+1). For odd n, in the second-neighbor cycle an original first step has distance (n-1)/2, and the second-only endpoint is optimal exactly at t<=S/J((n-1)/2)=16/(n^2+7). The even right endpoint is disconnected, and the objective has positive scalar second derivative on the connected interval, giving the stated unique mixed root and boundary classification. These exact computations cover all n>=5; no uploaded code was executed.
residual_risks: The supplied test is finite (n=5 through 11); the trace-vs-Fourier comparison is floating point, while the derivative and matrix finite differences use rationals. The exact proof, not the test, bears the all-n claim.

value.rationale: The result settles exactly when a whole edge class can be discarded in a standard cyclic network without worsening the globally optimal all-pairs resistance. The even and odd distinction and the different limiting price scales affect the design decision; exact support/equality thresholds and a unique interior characterization are useful beyond computing the resistance of one fixed allocation.
